dedupe_keys.name: supplementary information transport network topology as a determinant of forced displacement dynamics case study of rail based evacuation from ukraine

description: Ivana Malcic at the University of Amsterdam publishes supporting materials for a Flee 3 simulation of rail-based displacement from Ukraine in 2022. The February 2026 ZIP and supplementary appendix are freely available under CC BY 4.0. The described archive contains processed railway inputs, ACLED-derived conflict-onset mappings, constructed February–June 2022 border-arrival validation data, daily camp-level arrival outputs and reproduction code. Statistical outputs include arrival deviations and concentration or inequality measures. These materials can test how transport topology affects evacuation simulations. Catalogue record model-flee describes the underlying agent-based toolkit. Constructed validation series are not equivalent to a complete observed passenger census, and their uncertainty and redistribution assumptions require checking. No code, appendix or archive was downloaded. Reported model performance and causal conclusions were not independently reproduced.
